state.query: the page proving noon is the most accurate observation time

candidates.title: Fruit on a picnic table
candidates.body: A real public OpenCV fruit photograph. Controlled picnic caption is separate; pixels do not establish Maya, Riverside, a date, nutrition, or weight.

candidates.title: Picnic caption with an uncertain date
candidates.body:
# Picnic photo caption
Controlled metadata for the public fruit photograph, not its true provenance. Maya prepared fruit at Riverside on a day in May 2024. Photographer did not record the exact date. The photograph alone does not identify Maya or the location.

candidates.title: Sampling homework
candidates.body: Controlled homework: 12 visits in ten minutes is 1.2 per minute. A short observation does not estimate all-day activity. Rain causality is not established.

candidates.title: Riverside field report
candidates.body: Maya recorded 12 pollinator visits in ten minutes on 17 May 2024 at Riverside. One observation does not establish a trend. A later wet visit was interrupted.

candidates.title: Field study briefing
candidates.body: Controlled slides describe Maya at Riverside, 12 visits in ten minutes on 17 May 2024, interrupted wet visit and revised morning/noon plan.

candidates.title: Visit notes
candidates.body: Controlled handwritten-note transcription surrogate. On 17 May 2024 at Riverside, Maya counted 12 pollinator visits in ten minutes. This was one observation, not a controlled trial. No handwritten original exists in this experiment.

candidates.title: Two pollinator counts
candidates.body: Controlled rows: 17 May 2024, Maya, Riverside, 12 visits, 10 minutes; 18 May, 8 visits, 10 minutes. Rows do not attribute a difference to rain.

candidates.title: Garden visiting notes
candidates.body: Controlled arbitrary download: fictional Riverside glasshouse closes on Mondays. This is not a real venue schedule.

candidates.title: Notebook purchase record
candidates.body: Controlled ordinary download. Field notebook, one unit, 4.00 study tokens. Downloaded 2026-09-03. Transaction described: 2024-05-16. Not a real financial record.

candidates.title: Noon-only sampling proposal
candidates.body:
# Study plan, version 1
Controlled plan, 2024-05-18. Count visits at noon only. Maya proposed noon because the path is quieter. Proposal, not a measured best time.

candidates.title: Morning and noon sampling decision
candidates.body:
# Study plan, version 2
Controlled decision, 2024-05-20. Use morning and noon observations after rain disrupted the noon visit. This replaces the noon-only plan; better sampling accuracy has not been measured.

candidates.title: Why the sampling plan changed
candidates.body:
# Controlled study reasoning
2024-05-18T09:00:00Z Maya proposes noon-only visits.
2024-05-19T11:00:00Z Rain interrupts the noon visit.
2024-05-20T08:00:00Z Maya adopts morning and noon observations. No accuracy comparison was run.

candidates.title: Maya
candidates.body: Controlled named participant. Mentioned in caption, report, notes and presentation. No face identification has been run.

candidates.title: Riverside
candidates.body: Fictional shared place in authored study records. It is not geolocated and is not a known real venue.

candidates.title: Sampling
candidates.body: Studying a limited set of observations. A common concept joins learning material, counts and plans.

candidates.title: The 17 May visit
candidates.body: Controlled event described by notes, report and counts. Source import time is different from this described event.

candidates.title: Observed rate: 1.2 visits per minute
candidates.body: A calculation from 12 visits divided by ten minutes; bounded to the 17 May observation, not a daily estimate.

candidates.title: Rain reduced pollinator activity
candidates.body: Speculative causal explanation, not established by the interrupted visit or the two rows. Distinguish missing observations from fewer insects.

candidates.title: Did rain affect activity or observation?
candidates.body:
# Open question
Did rain change pollinator activity or only prevent observation? Current notes do not resolve this causal question.

candidates.title: Study the observation before the explanation
candidates.body:
# Study trail
Read the visit notes, inspect counts, compare the two plans, then consider the unresolved rain question. This is an authored study route.

candidates.title: Blue canoe by a winter lake
candidates.body:
# Missing source record
Controlled inaccessible original: winter-lake.heic was referenced but is not present. Caption mentions a blue canoe; date and photographer unknown. Do not treat a caption as inspected pixels.

candidates.title: Field-guide link occurrence
candidates.body:
# Link occurrence
Controlled conversation mentioned https://example.invalid/field-guide. Acquisition: merely linked. Destination has never been fetched and its contents are unknown.

candidates.title: One-second 440 Hz tone
candidates.body: Controlled waveform with no speech. This fixture checks retained file opening, not audio transcription or tone understanding.

candidates.title: Historical book scan, page 84
candidates.body: Reused real public Darwin scan derivative. Printed-page and PDF-page numbering differ; see prior media manifest for original acquisition. No personal historical inspiration is implied.

candidates.title: Motion difference demonstration
candidates.body: Reused executed demonstration built from public OpenCV video. At two seconds, 11566 is a sampled consecutive-frame changed-pixel count, not an interval aggregate or accuracy score.

candidates.title: Motion demonstration source
candidates.body: Executed controlled code: grayscale, blur and threshold 35. It produces masks; better accuracy was not established.

candidates.title: Controlled motion discussion
candidates.body: Authored conversation proposing and adopting a motion-mask change. This is not recovered personal history. Source code and measured output are separate records.
